newsitem.title: GERMANY: North German farmers plan swift beet plantings.
newsitem.headline: North German farmers plan swift beet plantings.

text.p: Farmers in Germany's north are now planting sugarbeet and hope to finish within a few days, an official at the Lower Saxony farm union said in response to an inquiry.
Farmers in this key growing region faced an involuntary delay of two weeks in the second half of March when initially mild and dry weather turned cold and rainy.
German beet plantings so far had been restricted to a few scattered regions in the south west, where the weather is especially warm.
The delay to the bulk of the crop would not be unusual or damaging as long as sowings were completed by mid-April, the Lower Saxony source said.
Lower Saxony in the 1996/97 campaign accounted for 6.204 million tonnes of a national beet delivery figure of 26.064 million.
This was more than in the whole of former eastern Germany, where 6.196 million were harvested.
Farmers in this northern region were also preparing potatoes and maize plantings after completing spring grains in early March, the source added.
Spring grains, winter grains and rapeseed had been developing well until mid-March when growth was slowed by the temporary return to cold weather.
But the crops were now catching up.
Warmer temperatures were already attracting pests, especially to winter rapeseed.
